summary_en: This study tests whether AGuIX gadolinium-based nanoparticles make stereotactic radiation work better for brain metastases that are harder to control with radiation alone. It includes several cancer types that have spread to the brain, such as melanoma, lung, breast, and gastrointestinal cancers. The nanoparticles or a placebo are given by intravenous injection 3-5 days before radiation and up to two times during radiation, depending on the radiation schedule. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a Phase II, double-blind, randomized study.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si las nanopartículas basadas en gadolinio AGuIX hacen que la radiación estereotáctica funcione mejor en metástasis cerebrales que son más difíciles de controlar solo con radiación. Incluye varios tipos de cáncer que se han extendido al cerebro, como melanoma y cánceres de pulmón, mama y gastrointestinales. Las nanopartículas o un placebo se administran por inyección intravenosa 3 a 5 días antes de la radiación y hasta dos veces durante la radiación, según el esquema de radiación. El desenlace principal no se indica en el registro; se trata de un estudio de Fase II, doble ciego y aleatorizado.
who_for: Biopsy-proven solid cancer with at least one brain lesion 5 mm or larger.
Melanoma growing despite immunotherapy, a gastrointestinal primary, or HER2-positive breast cancer.
Cystic brain metastases, or metastases 2 cm or larger.
Local recurrence after prior stereotactic or whole brain radiation.
Age 18 or older, kidney filtration of 60 or higher, Karnofsky score of 70 or higher, and expected survival of at least 3 months.
not_for: Cannot have a brain MRI or cannot receive gadolinium.
Need for radiation to more than 10 targets (or more than 20 after prior whole brain radiation).
Prior brain radiation with active metastases near the brainstem, eyes, optic nerves, or optic chiasm that exceed the stated dose limits.
